overview: This table tells the game which costume and facial expression pictures to show for each character in story scenes.
description: Maps story-demo character ids to ordered costume-row ids used to resolve the portrait and facial textures drawn by story-demo sequencer character images.

ID.simple: Choose the character who gets this story portrait setup.
ID.technical: Native FName Id; the supplied export spells the key `ID` and declares ImportKeyField as `Id`. All 14 exported row keys are unique and equal their ID values (CP_010 through CP_150, plus CN_122). GameStoryDemoImage_FindClothesRow passes the caller's CharacterId to FindRow on ScriptCharacterDataTables (DTM +0xA60), scanning table order and stopping at the first match with the missing-row warning disabled; the row's own `Id` member is not read. SetCharacter rejects NAME_None before this lookup. The id is authored on UAbramsSequencerStoryDemoCharacterParameterSection::CharacterId, whose C++ default is NAME_None.

Id_ScriptCharacterClothes.simple: Choose which costume and expression pictures appear for this character in story scenes, and in what order. A blank choice leaves that portrait without either picture.
Id_ScriptCharacterClothes.technical: TArray<FName>. The sequencer section's zero-based int32 ClothesIndex (C++ default 0) is checked with IsValidIndex before `Character->Id_ScriptCharacterClothes[ClothesIndex]` is taken; an out-of-range index returns no clothes row. The chosen id is looked up across ScriptCharacterClothesDataTables (DTM +0xA70), with the first matching table winning. NAME_None is passed through and finds no row in the supplied export; a missing row leaves the clothes texture null. The separate uint8 Facial argument indexes the resolved clothes row's FacialFileName array, not this array. Every supplied row has exactly four slots: 27 non-None ids, all of which resolve to ScriptCharacterClothesDataTable rows, and 29 None slots.

notes: Row constructor is empty; no default costume ids are injected in C++ (Source/AbramsDataTable/Private/GameDataTableRow_ScriptCharacter.cpp:3).

The manager registers one DataTable primary-asset loader named ScriptCharacterDataTable (Source/Abrams/Private/GameDataTableManager.cpp:469), resolves it after all loads complete, and appends it to the single-element ScriptCharacterDataTables array while skipping null tables (GameDataTableManager.cpp:146-158, 296). The clothes helper is the only source consumer of that cache; SetCharacter calls it twice, once for the clothes texture and once for the facial texture. First matching table wins if additional tables are ever present; the supplied export has one table and no duplicate row keys.

The only identified consumer is the story-demo portrait path. No direct Blueprint call is claimed, and the shipped Blueprint/UMG animation asset values that author CharacterId and ClothesIndex were not supplied; the available Content is partial.

The supplied datatables directory contains one ScriptCharacterDataTable asset with 14 rows and no numbered shards or localization variants. All 27 non-None costume ids resolve uniquely in the supplied ScriptCharacterClothesDataTable; the 29 None entries are explicit data sentinels rather than constructor defaults.

Runtime behavior is described from reconstructed C++ and exported data. The helper (retail 0x166e880) and SetCharacter (0x1685ad0) are BEHAV-certified but not byte-matched; the sequencer evaluate (0x179c360) is byte-matched. No retail Blueprint asset, retail runtime, or editor inspection was performed, so this is not an exhaustive claim about retail or Blueprint use.

usages.detail: Registers ScriptCharacterDataTable as a DataTable primary asset.
Resolves the loaded asset and appends it to ScriptCharacterDataTables (DTM +0xA60).
Scans the ScriptCharacterDataTables cache in order and stops at the first row found for CharacterId.
Rejects a missing character row or an out-of-range ClothesIndex before indexing this field.
Indexes this field and looks up the resulting FName across ScriptCharacterClothesDataTables (DTM +0xA70), returning the first match.
SetCharacter uses the resolved clothes row's ClothesFileName; a null or None result clears the clothes texture.
Repeats the same lookup for FacialFileName[Facial], where Facial is a separate uint8 sequencer channel value.
Supplies CharacterId, ClothesIndex and Facial from the evaluated UMG sequencer section to SetCharacter; the widget slot comes from sorted section CharacterIndex values.
